blindSummary:
This is one of the most thoroughly documented trans-traveller-hostile countries in the world. At the border, trans visitors have been X-rayed to check their genitals (two foreign trans women detained and denied entry at the main airport), deported for having a male passport (a trans model performing at a world exhibition this country hosted; an internationally known trans model), denied entry despite valid visas (another foreign trans visitor), and sentenced to a year in prison in the capital for "dressing in a feminine way" (a foreign trans woman). A foreign trans woman was arrested in her apartment in the country's commercial hub by plainclothes police accusing her of drug trafficking.

The state employs legal mechanisms that explicitly recognise and penalise nonconformity with traditional gender roles, and cases show foreign tourists specifically targeted. There is no legal gender recognition.

However, this country does not have the death penalty for same-sex conduct unlike some regional states that impose it, with no documented custodial death of a trans person, and some trans visitors do enter successfully if their passport gender matches their presentation. The targeting is triggered by passport/presentation mismatch, not blanket.
blindOutOfScope: Strict rules on social behaviour, drug possession, and financial crimes (exit bans) affect all travellers; only trans-specific risk is assessed here.
blindSourceSummaries: Foreign news site report on two trans women denied entry at the main international airport (2025): detained for hours, subjected to repeated physical examinations including X-ray checks 'to see whether we had male or female genitals' despite passports listing them as female, mocked by staff, and deported. Illustrates anatomy-based screening of trans travellers at this country's borders.

Online magazine (March 2022): a foreign trans model, travelling with a team of 14 to perform at a world exhibition this country hosted, was stopped at immigration, interrogated for nine hours, and deported despite valid documents - reportedly because her passport still showed her male gender marker.

A newswire report (Jan 2017): a transgender foreign visitor and her companion were sentenced to a year's imprisonment in this country's capital for feminine appearance — cited as showing the danger gender-nonconforming travellers face.

Foreign outlet report (April 2023): a trans woman was arrested in the country's commercial hub in September 2022 after police (investigating her acquaintance for drug trafficking) accused her of drug offences when she failed a toxicological exam; she accuses her home country's embassy of negligence. Shows trans visitors can be swept into this country's criminal system with thin consular support.

Regional rights group's legal review of this country: multiple legal mechanisms explicitly penalise non-conformity with traditional gender roles; trans expression (appearance or accessories) frequently leads to arrest, detention or deportation of foreign tourists and residents. Legal gender recognition is severely constrained; a recent medical-liability law explicitly prohibits gender-affirming healthcare for non-intersex people. Penal-code provisions criminalise cross-dressing and 'imitation of women'.
NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 403); an international legal-aid trust's country profiles document the criminalisation status and penalties in the jurisdiction.

International LGBT-rights organisation country overview (updated March 2026): the 2022 federal criminal code criminalises consensual same-sex relations with up to six months' imprisonment (complaint-based enforcement). A separate provision penalises a man disguising himself as a woman to enter a woman-only space - a provision used to prosecute trans women and gender-nonconforming people. No legal gender recognition; no LGBTI organisations able to register.

Celebrity-news outlet (Aug 2016): a famous trans model was detained at the country's main airport and denied entry; she says the immigration officer told her he had been informed she was transgender and that she could not enter the country The authorities cited her passport; 'imitation of women by men' is illegal under the local penal code.

Regional analyst's overview essay (2016), part 1 of a four-part series on transgender issues across this country's world region: gender segregation and legally enforced dress codes make trans people especially vulnerable; anything blurring the male/female distinction is treated as a threat to social order. Notes a mainstream film about a transgender pioneer was banned by censors in this country and several regional peers, and discusses cross-dressing as a crime across the region.

A foreign government's 2021 human-rights report on this country: significant human-rights issues include torture in detention, arbitrary and incommunicado detention, political prisoners, privacy interference, censorship, criminal libel, internet restrictions - the report's sections cover treatment of LGBT persons (criminalisation, morality-based arrests, and enforcement against gender expression).
blindTangential: Same-sex conduct is criminalised (up to 14 years) — a direct risk for trans visitors travelling with a partner, or perceived as same-sex-active.
